newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PTI agency has new chief, expands overseas.
newsitem.headline: India's PTI agency has new chief, expands overseas.

text.p: The Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Monday that Shobhana Bhartia, executive director of the Hindustan Times newspaper, was elected chairperson of the news agency.
PTI said Bhartia was unanimously elected at a meeting of the agency's board of directors in Bombay.
She succeeds C.R. Irani, editor-in-chief of the Statesman newspaper, who told the agency's annual general meeting that PTI planned to expand its international news operations.
Irani said PTI planned to open news bureaux in Cairo and Bonn and "cover as much of our world with our own correspondents as our resources will allow".
PTI is controlled by Indian newspapers and, along with United News of India, is one of two main domestic news agencies.
Currently PTI has overseas bureaux in Beijing, Colombo, Dhaka, Dubai, Islamabad, Kathmandu, London and Singapore.
Irani said PTI had joined four other news services in the Asia-Pacific region to start Asia Pulse, a service providing information on business opportunities in the region.
PTI quoted Irani as saying the service would be "of increasing value to our businessmen and industrialists seeking markets in the countries of the region".
The four other news services in Asia Pulse are AAP Information Services Pty Ltd of Australia, Indonesia's Antara news agency, Japan's Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc and South Korea's Yonhap, PTI said.
The outgoing chairman said PTI was exploring other opportunities to expand operations.
